body.statement: The mechanisms in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are strictly positive and rational and induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), whose latent projections are \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i\), with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\})\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}\). Both models therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\). Moreover \(P_{\sigma}(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)=r_a\) and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)=1/2\), while \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\). Hence \(P_{\sigma}(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)=3/64\), \(P_{\sigma}(S_i=1)=3/8\), and the two full selected observational laws assign probability \(1/8\) to every observed cell. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), \(P_+(Y_i=1)=9/16\), \(P_-(Y_i=1)=7/16\), and both selection normalizers equal \(3/8\). At the root role state, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1;0)=1/2\), whereas \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)=9/32\) and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)=7/32\), so the conditional effects are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\). The connected \(C_i\) is informative before selection because \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\neq1/4=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)\). The pair \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) consists of nested \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\)-rooted C-forests, with \(V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\})\); \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\), so they form the terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\). Finally, replacing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) by \(1/2\) preserves the graph and equality of the two selected observational laws but yields denominators \(25/41\) and \(23/39\); therefore the displayed denominator equality is a tuned informative cancellation, not a structural consequence of the graph.
body.justification: The proposition instantiates the general selection-equalizer lift with informative common child and selection kernels, verifies the represented graph and terminal forest, and exhibits exact positive locked denominators with separated numerators.
body.gap: Selected hedges alone do not coordinate the conditioning denominator; this example supplies a connected exact instance and a same-graph perturbation proving that the equality is tuned rather than forced by separation.
body.consumer: The table is a positive-control certificate for rational selected-hedge synthesis and verifies the general equalizer formulas with exact arithmetic.
body.proof_tex:
All variables in the informative-lock template are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their Bernoulli complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\}.
\]
Thus every local-table entry is rational and strictly between zero and one, as required by \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\), and binary support is supplied by \(\text{ass:binary-certificate-support}\).  The conditional law of \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\).  For either sign \(\sigma\), the conditional law of \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\).  The conditional law of \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\), and that of \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Consequently every displayed parent is active, and the induced directed graph is exactly \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

We next check the two projections in the informative graph-certificate definition.  Marginalizing \(U_i\) preserves \(X_i\to Y_i\) and induces \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) from \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the arrows \(Y_i\to C_i\), \(Y_i\to S_i\), and \(C_i\to S_i\) remain.  Every other path between nonadjacent vertices has an observed internal vertex, and hence creates no additional latent-projection edge.  The selected acyclic directed mixed graph is therefore precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

For the selected latent projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the endpoint marks on the adjacencies \(X_i-Y_i\) and \(Y_i-C_i\) are tails.  There is no \(X_i-C_i\) adjacency: in the relevant ancestral moral graph, after conditioning on and removing \(Y_i\) and \(S_i\), the vertex \(C_i\) is disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.                 \tag{1}
\]
The three-vertex noncollider chain has no invariant endpoint mark in its input-free equivalence class, so its completed partial graph is
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}
 =X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i
       \mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i.
\]
These direct projection and equivalence-class checks give
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \qquad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \qquad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}. \tag{2}
\]
Combining binary support, strict rational positivity, (2), and \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) yields
\[
 \mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}). \tag{3}
\]

We now compute the observational and interventional laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\), the denominators below are \(P(X_i=a)=1/2>0\), and Bayes' rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,
 &P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,
 &P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{4}
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the law of total probability and the outcome table in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
   \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a)\right\}
   P(U_i=u\mid X_i=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12,                 \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality uses (4).  Hence both signs have the same unselected observed law and
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for every }a,b\in\{0,1\}.                  \tag{6}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), SCM modularity removes the local factor for \(X_i\) and leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}. \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]

The appended \(C_i,S_i\) tables instantiate \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\).  Namely, set
\[
 g_b(d):=P(C_i=d\mid Y_i=b),
 \qquad \lambda_0=\lambda_1:=\frac3{16},
 \qquad \Lambda:=\lambda_0+\lambda_1=\frac38.          \tag{8}
\]
For every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 g_b(d)P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b,C_i=d)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{9}
\]
Moreover \(0<3/16<1/4=\min_b g_b(d)\) for both \(d\), so every positivity premise of that lemma holds.  Both appended parent relations are active, as checked above, so its graph qualification holds as well.  Applying its observational identity to (6) yields
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac14\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.                         \tag{10}
\]
There are eight observed cells; summing (10) gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8>0\).  Division by this normalizer gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{11}
\]
Thus the two complete selected observational laws coincide and have full support.

The interventional identities in \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\), together with (7)--(8), give the common terminal selection normalizer \(3/8\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac12,\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac9{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac9{32},\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac7{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac7{32}.    \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
The common conditioning denominator in (12) is strictly positive.  Dividing each numerator by it gives conditional causal effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), respectively.  The common \(C_i\) table also gives
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14
 =P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),                                   \tag{13}
\]
so the connected conditioning vertex is informative before selection.

It remains to verify the terminal forest assertions in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  The graph \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Also
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},
 \qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.          \tag{14}
\]
After intervention on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) belongs to the terminal set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Hence
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{15}
\]
For the maximal selection-exchange coordinate, \(S=\{S_i\}\), so the only nonempty candidate is \(D=\{S_i\}\).  In the corresponding input-augmented graph, the path
\[
 I_{S_i}\longrightarrow S_i\longleftarrow C_i           \tag{16}
\]
is open when conditioning on \(S_i\): its only internal vertex is a conditioned collider, and it has no noncollider at which the path could be blocked.  Thus \(I_{S_i}\) and \(C_i\) fail the required id-separation, making \(\{S_i\}\) inadmissible.  The empty set is admissible vacuously and is the only remaining subset.  Consequently
\[
 D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing.                     \tag{17}
\]
The bidirected-connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and maximal-exchange checks (14)--(17) are exactly the terminal selected-hedge predicates named in the informative graph-certificate definition.  Thus \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\).

Finally, consider the same-graph alternative \(\widetilde P\) from \(\text{sym:Alt}\), obtained by changing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The altered success probability and its complement are strictly positive rational numbers.  At fixed \(C_i=0\), the selection table still changes with \(Y_i\), and at fixed \(Y_i=0\), it still changes with \(C_i\); hence both arrows into \(S_i\) remain active and the represented graph is unchanged.  Equations (4)--(6) are unaffected, so the two signs retain the same unselected observed law.  Their \(C_i\) and modified \(S_i\) mechanisms are common; factorization therefore gives equal unnormalized selected observational masses cell by cell, and normalization gives equal full selected observational laws.

Put \(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\).  When \(Y_i=0\), summing the two unchanged products in (9) gives \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=0)=3/8\).  When \(Y_i=1\), the \(C_i=0\) product remains \(3/16\), whereas the modified \(C_i=1\) product is \((3/4)(1/2)=3/8\); hence \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=9/16\).  It follows by the law of total probability that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 \widetilde P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.            \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first quantity in (18) is positive.  Therefore the modified selected conditioning denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma(1;0)
 =\frac{3+3p}{6+3p}=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.                    \tag{19}
\]
Substituting \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (7) gives
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},
 \qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39}.                         \tag{20}
\]
These fractions differ because \(25\cdot39=975\ne943=23\cdot41\).  Hence equality of the denominators in (12) is the tuned informative cancellation supplied by (8)--(9), rather than a structural consequence of the represented graph.  This proves every assertion of the proposition.
